ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: everyday pressures
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Small, fixable things that wear on colonists: the same meal, the same work, someone away, a packed room, half-built work.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Two or three kinds of meal in the cooking bills keep the most common pressure away.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description:
A colony that has everything still has its everyday wear: the same stew every night, the same job every day, someone dear off on a long trip. Rimfolk adds five such pressures. Each is small, 1 to 3 mood, lasts only while its cause does, and says in its tooltip what caused it. The Mood tab says what helps. One has a good side: a varied table lifts the mood a little.
None of them is a flat penalty. A well-kept colony hardly feels them, and fixing them is ordinary colony work: a second meal bill, a second job in the Work tab, a bigger dining room.
Pressures wear on a colony that runs without care. Setbacks are what goes wrong even in one that doesn't: work wrecked in a raid, a field lost to blight, an operation gone wrong, a friend fallen ill. They follow the same setting and the same standards, and have a page of their own.

li.heading: The pressures

table.li: Pressure | When | Mood | Spared | What helps

The same meal | 6 of the last 8 meals the same kind; 10 of 12, then 12 of 12, for more | -1 to -3 | Ascetics, anyone whose faith allows only one kind of food, and fine or lavish meals; gourmands mind it a step more | Two or three kinds of meal in the bills
A varied table | 3 different foods in the last 2 days | +2 | Ascetics don't notice it | Keep the mix going

The same work | 70% of a day's working hours on one kind of work, 4, 7 and 10 days running | -1 to -3 | The industrious and hard-working, children, a burning passion for that work; any passion for it makes it a step lighter | A second kind of work, even a few hours a day
Missing someone | A partner apart for 2, 5 and 10 days; a close friend for 3 and 8 | -1 to -3 | Psychopaths and recluses don't miss friends | Being together again, shorter trips

A packed room | 4 or more people in a dining or rec room with too little space, or diners short of seats | -1 to -2, for half a day | Children; recluses mind it a step more | A bigger room, more seats, meals spread over the day
Half-built work | Frames untouched for 2 days in the home area | -1 to -3 | The lazy and slobs; the neat and industrious mind it a step more | Finish what's waiting, cancel the rest

li.after: Slaves, babies and guests feel none of them.

li.heading: Meals and the colony's era
li.text: What counts as the same meal depends on what the colony can cook. With only one kind of meal within reach, it comes up only after 8 of the same in a row, and goes no further than the first step; with two kinds it stops at the second. Meals, pemmican, berries and the like count. Fine and lavish meals never do: eating well every day is no rut. Nutrient paste, raw meat and vegetables, and other food the game already minds don't, so a bad meal is never counted twice. Meals are noted through one of Rimfolk's deeper game hooks; with those turned off, the same meal and the varied table never come up.

li.heading: Crowds and loose ends
li.text:
A room is crowded with 4 or more people in it and less than 4 cells of room each, and packed with less than 2.5. In a dining room, 2 diners without a seat make it crowded; when half of those eating (3 at least) have none, it's packed. Parties, rituals and council meetings don't count: being packed in is the point.
Only half-built frames count: 3 waiting frames are the first step, 10 the second and 25 the third. Plans (blueprints) never count, so lay out as much in advance as you like.

table.li: Gentle | Half strength, never less than 1 | 70% | Half-built work and the fussiest setbacks aren't minded; standards don't make frictions sting more
Normal | 85% of the table above, never less than 1 | 85% | Spoiled colonists feel pressures and frictions up to 40% more
Demanding | Half again as strong | As written | As normal

li.heading: Hard times
li.text: People go easier on someone who is struggling. As a colonist's mood nears the line where they could break, Rimfolk's own small letdowns (a joke that fell flat, being talked about, a bad moment at the table, a sticking door) weigh less, down to half at the line, and its pressures down to three quarters. It starts 15 points above their minor-break line and goes back to normal as they recover, so it steadies a bad stretch without hiding what's wrong: the pressures still say what to fix. Low spirits bring nightmares only a little more often, though sweet dreams still come rarely.

li.heading: Standards and the heart
li.text:
As colonists' standards rise, the council's rewards shrink, the game's own comforts count for less (down to 70% for the spoiled), and the colony's own frictions, nuisances and pressures sting more: up to 40% more for the spoiled. A colony that stays content for seasons has more to keep up with.
The pressures also feed the heart's feelings. Missing someone feeds loneliness, the same work or meal feeds restlessness, a packed room or half-built work feeds frustration, and a varied table feeds contentment.
